run-the-checks.text: From the repository root, run the root build gate. From offchain, run the lint app and classified component build. The root gate does not compile every offchain Cabal component. The component carrier compiles the library, tests, and components required by current workflows and supported commands without executing them. Its current measured inventory classifies all twenty Cabal declarations: eleven are compiled here — the library, the private node ownership core the library links, and the supported commands and tests — and nine retained commands stay unverified under their owning issues. An included member failure fails the carrier; its green result is not a package-wide build.

where-the-source-list-comes-from.text: The lint app reads every source-directory declaration in the cabal file at run time and adds the two naming directories whose scripts compile them directly with GHC. It deduplicates nested directories and fails if discovery finds no sources or a declared directory is absent.

The source-derived inventory at the ticket 267 candidate measures 89 discovered Haskell files in 23 source directories: Fourmolu selects 87 after the two verifier exclusions, and HLint selects 76 within ten directories. The added end-to-end witness belongs to all three sets. At ae4fe9a, the lint app passed in the final Gate S off-chain lint row and in pushed-head continuous integration; that gate row reported 89 discovered files in 23 directories, Fourmolu over 87 files, and HLint over ten directories with no hints. These green receipts cover only the selected extents. At the ticket 270 candidate the same app reported 128 discovered files in 23 directories, Fourmolu over 126, and HLint over ten directories with no hints. The thirty new command modules sit inside already declared source directories, so discovery found them without a configuration change. Since ticket 278 slice two, the formatter runs under the house fourmolu yaml committed at the repository root, passed explicitly to every entrypoint so a missing configuration fails loudly instead of falling back to Fourmolu defaults, over every discovered offchain Haskell source with no exclusions: one hundred twenty-eight files at this writing, the two formerly fenced verifier sources included. HLint runs over the same files: the thirteen directories ticket 264 left outside it had their hints resolved at the source, and the exclusion list is gone. Compare the next actual lint output with this inventory.

The flake derives a supported build set from the current workflow and supported command closure. Its inventory must account for every Cabal library, executable, and test suite, and the gate must fail when a new declaration has no classification or an omitted classification drifts.

current-boundaries.text: The inventory, formatting, HLint and component build extents are separate. The two independent verifier sources left the ticket 264 source fence in 278 slice two: they are formatted and HLint-checked like every other Haskell source. Connected verifier stays declared and unverified under issue 282; its recorded build failures belong to earlier revisions of the project and its source still names identifiers the current library no longer exports. Retained journeys are unverified under issue 172 after source and workflow checks. Register rows is outside that journey retirement record and separately unverified under issue 283. The earlier carrier directly failed at recovery rows; it did not build each other omitted command. Under the release instruction correction, the archive readme and consumer guides present only the verified journey and checks as runnable and disclose all nine unverified declarations as retained; the local attach check script is a disclosed, currently unrunnable local gate. Neither Fourmolu nor HLint has directory exclusions; a retained journey that does not compile is still formatted and HLint-checked, and those checks say nothing about whether it builds. Compare the next actual lint output with this inventory rather than assuming a filename search proves coverage.

module-ownership-maps.text: The builder and blueprint modules, the node runtime, the registry fold, and the four registry commands now each have a contributor map: which module owns a concern, where common edits land, and which decisions the extraction recorded. They are Builder and blueprint modules, Node module ownership, Who owns a registry fold, and Who owns a registry command.
